title: Prime-chain bound from quotient colength polynomials and principal differences
statement:
Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a nonzero commutative Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. For every proper ideal $I\subset R$ put $A_I=R/I$, $\mathfrak m_I=\mathfrak m A_I$, and $H_I(n)=\mathrm{length}_{A_I}(A_I/\mathfrak m_I^n)$ for integers $n\ge1$ [def-weil-pbc-module-length]. Suppose each $H_I(n)$ is finite, and for every proper $I$ a nonzero polynomial $Q_I\in\mathbf Q[X]$ with positive leading coefficient is given such that $H_I(n)=Q_I(n)$ for all sufficiently large $n$ (the threshold may depend on $I$). Suppose also that for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ and every $x\in\mathfrak m\setminus\mathfrak p$ there is an integer $c\ge1$ such that, writing $J=\mathfrak p+(x)$,
$$H_J(n)\le H_{\mathfrak p}(n)-H_{\mathfrak p}(n-c)\qquad(n>c).$$
Then for all proper ideals $I\subseteq I'$ of $R$, $\deg Q_{I'}\le\deg Q_I$; for $\mathfrak p,x,J=\mathfrak p+(x)$ as above, $\deg Q_{\mathfrak p}\ge1$ and $\deg Q_J\le\deg Q_{\mathfrak p}-1$. For every proper ideal $I$, every strict chain of prime ideals in $R/I$ has length at most $\deg Q_I$. In particular $\dim R\le\deg Q_{(0)}$, where Krull dimension means the supremum of prime-chain lengths [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring].

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-local-ring-unit-criterion], every proper ideal of $R$ lies in $\mathfrak m$: if it contained $a\notin\mathfrak m$, it would contain the unit $a$, hence $1$. In particular every prime lies in $\mathfrak m$. If $x\in\mathfrak m\setminus\mathfrak p$, then $J=\mathfrak p+(x)\subseteq\mathfrak m$ is proper. For any proper $I$ and $n\ge1$, the module $A_I/\mathfrak m_I^n$ is nonzero: the ideal $\mathfrak m_I^n$ is contained in the proper ideal $\mathfrak m_I$ (the image of $\mathfrak m$ in $R/I$). Its chain $0\subsetneq A_I/\mathfrak m_I^n$ shows $H_I(n)\ge1$ by [def-weil-pbc-module-length].

source.place: Tag 00E9, lemma-characterize-local-ring, units outside the maximal ideal; Tag 02LY, definition-length, the length-one chain.

proof.text: For a proper $I$, identify $A_I/\mathfrak m_I^n$ with $R/(I+\mathfrak m^n)$: the image of $\mathfrak m^n$ is $\mathfrak m_I^n$, since both are generated by products of $n$ images of elements of $\mathfrak m$. Its $A_I$-submodules are exactly its $R$-submodules: lift any scalar of $A_I$ to $R$. Thus these two lengths agree. If $I\subseteq I'$ are proper, the map $R/(I+\mathfrak m^n)\twoheadrightarrow R/(I'+\mathfrak m^n)$ lifts every strict submodule chain in the target to a strict chain of inverse images in the source (surjectivity preserves strictness). Taking the suprema defining length [def-weil-pbc-module-length] gives $H_{I'}(n)\le H_I(n)$ for every $n\ge1$.

proof.text: We record the elementary coefficient estimate used below, with polynomial notions as in [def-weil-polynomial-ring]. If $F(T)=aT^d+\sum_{i<d}b_iT^i$, $a>0$, then for integers $n\ge1$ and $d\ge1$, $\left|\sum_{i<d}b_in^i\right|\le Bn^{d-1}$, where $B=\sum_{i<d}|b_i|$. Hence $F(n)\ge (a/2)n^d>0$ once $n\ge2B/a$; if $d=0$, $F(n)=a>0$. Consequently, for nonzero polynomials $P,Q$ with positive leading coefficients, an eventual inequality $P(n)\le Q(n)$ on integers implies $\deg P\le\deg Q$: otherwise $P-Q$ has degree $\deg P$ and positive leading coefficient, so the displayed estimate makes $P(n)-Q(n)>0$ for all sufficiently large integers, a contradiction.

source.place: Tag 00KQ, proposition-dimension, polynomial-degree comparisons; the elementary coefficient bound and subtraction argument are written out here.

proof.text: Fix proper $I\subseteq I'$. Choose an integer beyond the two eventual-equality thresholds for $Q_I,Q_{I'}$ and beyond $1$. Step 2 gives $Q_{I'}(n)\le Q_I(n)$ for every integer beyond this threshold. Both polynomials are nonzero with positive leading coefficients by hypothesis, so Step 3 gives $\deg Q_{I'}\le\deg Q_I$. Thresholds need not be uniform in $I$: only this pair is used.

source.place: Tag 00KQ, proposition-dimension, comparison of a ring and its prime quotient; the same comparison applies to every pair of proper ideals.

proof.text: Fix $\mathfrak p,x,J$ as in the statement and choose its $c\ge1$. Put $P=Q_{\mathfrak p}$, $D(T)=P(T)-P(T-c)$, and $d=\deg P$. Beyond the thresholds for $Q_J(n)$, $P(n)$ and $P(n-c)$, and with $n>c$, the assumed inequality reads $Q_J(n)\le D(n)$. If $d=0$, $D=0$, contradicting $Q_J(n)=H_J(n)\ge1$ from Step 1. Thus $d\ge1$. Expanding $(T-c)^i=\sum_{j=0}^i\binom{i}{j}T^j(-c)^{i-j}$ shows that the degree-$d$ coefficients cancel in $D$, its degree-$(d-1)$ coefficient is $dc\,\operatorname{lc}(P)>0$, and no higher coefficient remains; terms of $P$ of degree less than $d$ contribute differences of degree at most $d-2$. For $d=1$ their constant differences are zero. Therefore $D\ne0$ and $\deg D=d-1$.

proof.text: Apply Step 3 to $Q_J(n)\le D(n)$ from Step 5. The hypotheses hold: $Q_J$ is nonzero with positive leading coefficient by assumption; $D$ is nonzero with leading coefficient $dc\,\operatorname{lc}(P)>0$ by Step 5. This gives $\deg Q_J\le\deg D=\deg Q_{\mathfrak p}-1$, together with the already established $\deg Q_{\mathfrak p}\ge1$.

proof.text: For adjacent primes $\mathfrak p\subsetneq\mathfrak q$ of $R$, choose $x\in\mathfrak q\setminus\mathfrak p$. Step 1 gives $x\in\mathfrak m$ and $J=\mathfrak p+(x)\subseteq\mathfrak q$ proper. Steps 4 and 6 imply $\deg Q_{\mathfrak q}\le\deg Q_J\le\deg Q_{\mathfrak p}-1$. To treat a chain $\bar{\mathfrak p}_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\bar{\mathfrak p}_r$ in $R/I$, take inverse images $\mathfrak p_i$ under $R\twoheadrightarrow R/I$. They are prime: if $ab$ maps into $\bar{\mathfrak p}_i$, primality there puts the image of $a$ or $b$ in it. They are proper, contain $I$, and strictness follows by lifting an element of each set difference. Thus each adjacent pair satisfies the displayed degree drop.

proof.text: Write $e_i=\deg Q_{\mathfrak p_i}\in\mathbb N$. Iterating the inequalities of Step 7 gives $e_r+r\le e_0$: for a chain with no inclusions this is equality, and each additional inclusion contributes $e_{i+1}+1\le e_i$. Since $e_r\ge0$ and Step 4 gives $e_0\le\deg Q_I$, we obtain $r\le\deg Q_I$. This also handles $\deg Q_I=0$: a positive-length chain would force $1\le0$. Finally $(0)$ is proper because $R\ne0$; applying the bound with $I=(0)$ and taking the supremum of all prime-chain lengths gives $\dim R\le\deg Q_{(0)}$ by [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring].

lean.statement: theorem primeChain_bound_of_colength_polynomials (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R] (Q : Ideal R → Polynomial ℚ) (hfinite : ∀ (I : Ideal R), I ≠ ⊤ → ∀ (n : ℕ), 1 ≤ n → quotientPowerColength I n < ⊤) (hpoly : ∀ (I : Ideal R), I ≠ ⊤ → Q I ≠ 0 ∧ 0 < (Q I).leadingCoeff ∧ ∃ N : ℕ, 1 ≤ N ∧ ∀ (n : ℕ), N ≤ n → ((quotientPowerColength I n).toNat : ℚ) = (Q I).eval (n : ℚ)) (hdiff : ∀ (p : Ideal R), p.IsPrime → ∀ (x : R), x ∈ maximalIdeal R → x ∉ p → ∃ c : ℕ, 1 ≤ c ∧ ∀ (n : ℕ), c < n → (quotientPowerColength (p ⊔ Ideal.span {x}) n).toNat ≤ (quotientPowerColength p n).toNat - (quotientPowerColength p (n - c)).toNat) : (∀ (I I' : Ideal R), I ≠ ⊤ → I' ≠ ⊤ → I ≤ I' → (Q I').natDegree ≤ (Q I).natDegree) ∧ (∀ (p : Ideal R), p.IsPrime → ∀ (x : R), x ∈ maximalIdeal R → x ∉ p → 1 ≤ (Q p).natDegree ∧ (Q (p ⊔ Ideal.span {x})).natDegree ≤ (Q p).natDegree - 1) ∧ (∀ (I : Ideal R), I ≠ ⊤ → ∀ (s : LTSeries (PrimeSpectrum (R ⧸ I))), s.length ≤ (Q I).natDegree) ∧ ringKrullDim R ≤ ((Q ⊥).natDegree : WithBot ℕ∞)
